_note: ThusoIQ Core's closed loop and alert router, Wave 3: the rungs an alert is routed by and how long each has to be acknowledged, the codes an escalation and a snooze are given, who an unacknowledged concern goes to after its fallback, what a panic alerts, what happens when there is nobody left to escalate to, and the order the Control Tower reads concerns in. MyThuso Master Blueprint v4's Core table and ThusoIQ Master v3.5 §14 name what it must do: 'concern → owner → SLA → fallback → outcome', 'every alert has an owner and a response expectation', 'deduplication, suppression windows, severity tiers, snooze-with-reason'. The escalation rota and the minutes each post holds a concern are Core's settings, below, in the shape packages/catalog/settings.json gives every setting, because the founder instructed on 15 September 2026 that open questions become admin settings. packages/engines/src/core holds the arithmetic; every refusal sentence is packages/catalog/apis/core.json's. There is no emitter beside this file on purpose: no app renders Core, and the Control Tower reads it through GET /v1/core/loops@2. Nothing here is a running service. No alert reaches a person, no page is sent and nobody is on call.
_numbersNote: Every number below is a proposal. `decidedBy: null` means nobody with the authority to set it has set it. ThusoIQ Master v3.5 names the ladder's response times and its readiness review names the missing 'rota and authority matrix'; the numbers are here so the router can be built and tested against something, and the build refuses a proposal that loses its `decidedBy`, its question or why it was proposed. The rota and its minutes are settings, which an admin changes on the back office within bounds that are themselves proposals.

ladder.source: ThusoIQ Master v3.5 §13, Figure 8 — the escalation ladder
ladder.why: A rung is how urgent a concern is. It decides how long the owner has to acknowledge it and nothing else: moving a concern up a rung is a clinician's decision on the ladder, not the router's when a deadline passes, and a deadline that passes moves the concern to the next holder on its escalation — its fallback, then the posts of the rota.
ladder._notTheRotaNote: These rungs are not the rota's rungs, and escalation-minutes replaces none of them. acknowledgeWithinMinutes is how long an alert's first owner has to acknowledge it, by how urgent the alert is. escalation-minutes is how long each post on the rota holds a concern nobody has taken on before it goes to the next post, whatever the concern is. The five below answer the first question and are kept as they were; merging them with the second would make one number answer two questions, and the day one of them changed the other would change with it.

acknowledgeWithinMinutes.proposedBecause: The document says immediate, and a deadline of nought would move a concern on before anybody could press acknowledge. Five minutes is how long ThusoIQ Master v3.5's mental-health pathway lets a clinician be unreachable in a crisis before it goes to the next person, borrowed here for every rung the document calls immediate.
acknowledgeWithinMinutes.question: How long the owner of a rung-one concern has to acknowledge it.

acknowledgeWithinMinutes.proposedBecause: The document gives two response times for this rung, and an alert carries nothing that tells an urgent one from a critical one. Holding every rung-two alert to the critical time means an urgent one is acknowledged early; the other choice means a critical one waits two hours.
acknowledgeWithinMinutes.question: How long the owner of a rung-two concern has to acknowledge it, while an alert cannot say whether it is urgent or critical.

acknowledgeWithinMinutes.proposedBecause: The document's own figure for this rung.
acknowledgeWithinMinutes.question: How long the owner of a rung-three concern has to acknowledge it.

acknowledgeWithinMinutes.proposedBecause: As for rung one: immediate, with enough time to press acknowledge. Rung four hands to dispatch in the document, and nothing here dispatches.
acknowledgeWithinMinutes.question: How long the owner of a rung-four concern has to acknowledge it.

acknowledgeWithinMinutes.proposedBecause: As for rung one. Rung five tells the family in the document, and nothing here tells anybody.
acknowledgeWithinMinutes.question: How long the owner of a rung-five concern has to acknowledge it.

severities.source: ThusoIQ Master v3.5 §15 — routine (tier 2), moderate (tier 3), major or critical (tiers 4–5)
severities.why: Least severe first. They are the three words nok.notified@1's severityCode already carries, so the bus has one vocabulary for how bad a thing is. The highest the contract allows is the last.

fallbackDeadline.derivedFrom: The concern's own span: the deadline it was opened with, less the moment it was opened. An alert's span is its rung's acknowledgeWithinMinutes.
fallbackDeadline.lastPost: The last post on the rota is given the concern's own span too. escalation-minutes holds the time a post has before the next post, one fewer than there are posts, and there is no post after the last to hand the concern to.
fallbackDeadline.why: A fallback is given the time the owner was given. A second number for the fallback would be a second answer to how urgent the same concern is.

auditExport.why: GET /v1/core/audit-exports@1 refuses a range wider than a bound (range-too-wide), so an export is never a copy of the whole trail taken in one call. How wide is too wide is exactly the kind of open question the founder's instruction of 15 September 2026 turns into a setting rather than a number typed into the route, so it is here, beside the escalation settings, as the third thing Core's admin block holds.

order: The concern's owner, for its own span.
Its fallback, for the same span.
The posts of the rota it was opened under, in the setting's order, each for its minutes, and the last for the concern's own span.
escalation.fallbackRole: An extra rung before the rota, never rung one's override. The engine that opened the concern named its fallback, and the desk is asked after it all the same, so a concern loses neither. As an override the desk would never hear of a concern whose fallback was somebody else, which is the concern lost the moment that somebody did not answer.
escalation.onDuty: A post is asked only when one of its windows, in the rota the concern kept, covers the moment the concern reaches it: the day of the week and the time of day in packages/catalog/scheduling.json's timezone. A post that is not on duty, or that no role on the vetting register holds, is skipped and the skip is written to loop_audit, and the concern goes to the next post that is on duty. It is never handed to another role in that post's place.
escalation.keepsItsRota: A concern keeps the rota, the minutes and the settings version in force when it was opened, and never reads them again. An admin who changes the rota mid-afternoon changes where the next concern goes, and a concern already on its second rung carries on up the rota it started on.
escalation.why: ThusoIQ Master v3.5 says an unacknowledged concern goes 'to the next person on the rota'. The rota is who is on duty when, by post and never by name, and it is operations' to set, so it is a setting an admin changes rather than a list of roles guessed into this file.

panic.rule: A panic alerts every post on duty in the rota in force at once, and walks nothing: nobody is asked after anybody else, and nothing waits for minutes to pass before the next post hears it.
panic.notASetting: It is written here as a rule and in packages/engines/src/core as code, and not in the settings block, on purpose. A nurse who has pressed panic is in danger now, and a rota that walked her panic one post at a time would be a setting that decides how long she waits for the second person to hear. No admin may choose that, so no setting says it, and the build fails if one does.

ladderRung.proposedBecause: Sentinel Dispatch is the rung the document gives to somebody in danger now, and it says immediate. Every post a panic alerts has that rung's acknowledgeWithinMinutes to take it on before the panic is exhausted, so a panic is given the time the ladder already gives dispatch rather than a second number for the same urgency.
ladderRung.question: How long the posts a panic alerts have to take it on before nobody is left to escalate it to.

panic.why: panic.raised@1 already names Core among its subscribers. Core opens the panic as a concern with every post on duty as its holders, at the highest severity, and one panic is one concern however often the bus delivers it.

dedupe.window: While the alert it matches is open.
dedupe.why: Two alerts with one key are one alert for as long as the first is still open, and it is answered with suppressed: true and no event. A key raised again after its alert was closed is a new alert: that concern was closed with an outcome, and a concern that comes back is a concern again. A timed suppression window that swallows alerts after a close is not built — it would need a number somebody decides, and until then nothing is absorbed that is not already open.
dedupe.higherRung: An alert raised again at a higher rung than the open one is escalated to that rung, with alert.escalated@1 and the reason raisedAgainHigher. It is never lowered by being raised again at a lower one.

snooze.buys: One more span of the alert's own rung, from when it is snoozed.

value.means: The owner has contacted the patient and is waiting to hear back.
The owner is attending to another patient and will take this on next.

reasons.proposedBecause: Two reasons a nurse or a doctor gives for not acting yet that are about time and not about whether the concern matters. A reason that says the concern does not matter is a close, which needs an outcome.
reasons.question: The reasons an owner may give for snoozing an alert.

snooze.why: A snooze is a code from this list or it is refused. It is never given to a concern that has run out of people to escalate to, because a snooze there is a second way of nobody being told.

value.means: The owner has been tried and has not answered.
The owner has seen it and it needs somebody who can decide more.

byCaller.proposedBecause: The two reasons the desk moves a concern before its deadline: nobody answered, or the person who answered cannot decide it.
byCaller.question: The reasons the desk may give for escalating a concern before its deadline.

escalationReasons.why: A code, never free text: the reason travels on loop.escalated@1 and alert.escalated@1, and words on the bus are words with none of the record's protections.

value.label: Dealt with
value.means: Somebody who held it did what it needed. Where that is written down is the reference it was closed with, or the concern itself.

value.label: Raised in error
value.means: It should not have been raised, and nothing needed doing.

value.label: Handed to a service outside MyThuso
value.means: It was passed to a service MyThuso does not run, and is theirs now. Nothing here contacts that service.

outcomes.proposedBecause: Three things the desk says when it closes a concern that are about what happened and not about the person it concerned: it was dealt with, it should never have been raised, or it left MyThuso's hands. None names a condition, so none is clinical content on a screen or in loop_audit.
outcomes.question: The outcomes a concern may be closed with.
outcomes.why: POST /v1/core/loops/{loopRef}/close@2 takes one of these or refuses. An exhausted concern closes only with one too, because a concern nobody was left to escalate to is the one a review most needs to count.

closesAs.proposedBecause: Each of the outcomes Safety's desk resolves a panic with, in packages/catalog/field-safety.json, said as the closed loop's own: a nurse who was safe, with or without the desk speaking to her, is a concern dealt with; a person at the desk calling the police or an ambulance is a concern handed to a service outside MyThuso; a press confirmed as a mistake is a concern raised in error. None names what the visit was for.
closesAs.question: Which of the closed loop's outcomes the concern opened for a panic is closed as when Safety's desk resolves the panic.

panicResolved.why: Core opens a concern for every panic it hears, alerting every post on duty. When a person at Safety's desk resolves the panic, panic.resolved@1 carries the outcome's code, and Core closes that concern through the same closeRefusal rule the close route asks, with the outcome this map gives. A code the map does not name is not guessed at: the concern stays open for a person to close, and Core's audit says it was not stood down. The map lives here, beside the outcomes it names, because Core reads no Safety contract.

closesAs.proposedBecause: A clinician acknowledging a result is somebody who held the concern doing what it needed, which is what dealt-with means. Where it is written down is the result's own entry in the Health Passport, and the concern closes pointing at it.
closesAs.question: Which of the closed loop's outcomes the concern opened for an unacknowledged lab result is closed as when a clinician acknowledges the result.

resultAcknowledged.why: Medicines raises an alert with Core when a lab result arrives (POST /v1/core/alerts@2, justified by lab.result.received@1), with the result's Passport entry as its dedupe key and its record entry, on the rung its own settings name. When the clinician who ordered the test acknowledges the result, Clinical publishes result.acknowledged@1 naming the same entry, and Core stands the alert down: closed through the closeRefusal rule the close route asks, with the outcome named here, by the role that acknowledged it and pointing at the entry. Only an open alert that the engine alertsFrom names raised under that key is touched, and nothing else about it moves. An alert nobody acknowledges is never closed this way: it escalates up the rota like any other, because a result nobody read is the concern the closed loop exists for.

ownerRole.proposedBecause: The Control Tower operator is the desk, and the desk is where a patient's press is read: the door it went to, the area while it is shared, and whether next of kin could be told.
ownerRole.question: Who owns the concern Core opens when a patient presses SOS.

fallbackRole.proposedBecause: A registered nurse can judge what an SOS nobody has taken on needs, and the on-call nurse lead is on the rota around the clock.
fallbackRole.question: Who holds an SOS concern the desk has not taken on in time.

ladderRung.proposedBecause: Somebody asking for help now is the urgency the ladder gives Sentinel Dispatch, which it calls immediate. The desk is given that rung's time to take the concern on, as a panic's posts are, rather than a second number for the same urgency.
ladderRung.question: How long the desk has to take on an SOS concern before it goes to its fallback.

sos.rule: One SOS is one concern however often the bus delivers it: owned by the desk, falling back to a nurse, then walking the rota it was opened under. It opens for every door, emergency services and cannot-help included, because the desk needs to know somebody pressed. No plan changes its owner, its deadline or where the Control Tower reads it.
sos.why: sos.raised@2 names Core among its subscribers. Core reads no Safety contract and no plan: the owner, the fallback and the rung are proposals here, beside the rota they walk.

closesAs.proposedBecause: Each reason a person may stand an SOS down with, in packages/catalog/sos.json standDown, said as the closed loop's own: a press by mistake is a concern raised in error; a situation that settled is a concern dealt with; going to hospital themselves is a concern handed to a service outside MyThuso. None names what was wrong.
closesAs.question: Which of the closed loop's outcomes an SOS concern is closed as when the person who pressed it stands it down.

sosStoodDown.why: A stand-down closes the concern Core opened for the SOS through the same closeRefusal rule the close route asks, pointing at the SOS, by the role that stood it down. A reason the map does not name is not guessed at: the concern stays open for a person to close, and Core's audit says it was not stood down.

ownerRole.proposedBecause: A registered nurse is who calls a patient who has come home from hospital, checks that they understood the discharge and have their medicines, and books a visit when one is needed. The discharge itself is read in the record under her grant.
ownerRole.question: Who owns the follow-up concern Core opens when a hospital says a patient was discharged.

fallbackRole.proposedBecause: A doctor can judge what a discharge nobody has followed up needs, including whether it needs a visit today.
fallbackRole.question: Who holds a discharge follow-up concern the nurse has not taken on in time.

ladderRung.proposedBecause: Nurse review. A discharge is not an emergency, and rung three would page a clinician for every routine one; the nurse rung's time is the least the ladder gives a concern a nurse must read.
ladderRung.question: How long the nurse has to take on a discharge follow-up concern before it goes to its fallback.

dischargeReceived.rule: One discharge is one follow-up concern however often the bus delivers it, keyed by its encounter: owned by a nurse, falling back to a doctor, then walking the rota it was opened under. A person closes it with an outcome; no event closes it for them.
dischargeReceived.why: passport.discharge.received@1 names Core as its only subscriber. Core reads no Record contract: the owner, the fallback and the rung are proposals here, beside the rota they walk. The concern points at the encounter, and what the discharge says is read in the record.

opensAtRung.proposedBecause: Rung three is the ladder's Clinician alert. A tier one is recorded and a tier two is for the nurse's own queue, and neither pages anybody; a tier three is somebody a clinician must take on now, which is what a concern on the rota is for.
opensAtRung.question: From which Sentinel rung Core opens a concern on the escalation rota.

ownerRole.proposedBecause: A tier three is the ladder's Clinician alert, and a doctor is the clinician who can decide what it needs.
ownerRole.question: Who owns the concern Core opens for a Sentinel tier three.

fallbackRole.proposedBecause: A registered nurse can go to the patient, and the on-call nurse lead is on the rota around the clock.
fallbackRole.question: Who holds a Sentinel concern the doctor has not taken on in time.

sentinel.rule: One tier raised is one alert however often the bus delivers it, keyed by the concern Sentinel raised and pointing at the record entry it is about. Below opensAtRung Core opens nothing. The time to acknowledge it is the ladder's for the rung it was raised at, and nothing Sentinel sends chooses the owner, the fallback or the time.
sentinel.why: sentinel.rung_raised@1 names Core as its subscriber. Core reads no Safety contract: which rung opens a concern, and who owns it, are proposals here, beside the ladder whose times they use.

ownerRole.proposedBecause: The desk makes sure a safeguarding report reaches the safeguarding officer. Until that role is on the vetting register, the desk is the one place a report cannot go unnoticed.
ownerRole.question: Who owns the concern Core opens when a safeguarding concern is recorded.

fallbackRole.proposedBecause: The Head of Operations answers for a concern the desk did not take on, and a safeguarding report nobody took on is exactly that.
fallbackRole.question: Who holds a safeguarding concern the desk has not taken on in time.

ladderRung.proposedBecause: A recorded safeguarding concern is somebody who may be at risk and is not in danger this minute, because somebody in danger is pointed at emergency services first. Rung two gives the desk the ladder's urgent time rather than a second number.
ladderRung.question: How long the desk has to take on a safeguarding concern before it goes to its fallback.

safeguarding.rule: One report is one concern however often the bus delivers it, owned by the desk and falling back to the Head of Operations, then walking the rota it was opened under. Closing the concern says the desk took the report on; it never closes the report, which only a safeguarding officer could.
safeguarding.why: safeguarding.reported@2 names Core as its subscriber and carries the report and nothing else. Core reads no Safety contract: the owner, the fallback and the rung are proposals here.

_reasonsNotSettingsNote: The snooze reasons and the reasons the desk escalates by hand stay proposals in this file rather than becoming settings, on purpose. Each is a code that travels on the bus — alert.escalated@1 and loop.escalated@1 carry reasonCode — or is sent by an app a nurse already has. A code an admin added on the back office would be put on the bus to subscribers that were built and reviewed against the codes here and cannot read it; a code an admin removed would refuse the reason a nurse's phone still offers her. Neither is an admin choosing within bounds: both are a change to the contract every subscriber and every app is built against, made the way this file is changed. The question each asks stays open beside it until somebody with the authority answers it.

exhaustion._declaredInNote: Not declared in packages/catalog/events.json, deliberately. The event contract refuses a live event with no subscribers, and no engine hears an exhausted concern today: Safety, Care and Access have no handler for it, and listing one to satisfy the rule would be a subscriber that reads nothing. The Control Tower learns of an exhausted concern through GET /v1/core/loops@2, first in the list, and needs no subscriber. It is declared the day an engine acts on it. Until then the bus refuses it; Core keeps the concern exhausted anyway, writes down that it has not been announced, and tries again on every tick, so a refusal of the announcement never becomes a concern that quietly stopped.
exhaustion.when: A concern past its deadline, unacknowledged, with nobody after it: its fallback behind it and no post of the rota it was opened under left that is on duty and held by a role — or a panic nobody it alerted has taken on.
stays: first in what the Control Tower reads
exhaustion.why: Escalation goes to a concern's fallback and then up the rota it was opened under, and nowhere after the last post on duty. When that runs out, the honest thing is to say so loudly and keep saying it until a person closes the concern with an outcome.

controlTower.why: The concerns nobody is left to escalate to are the ones only the Control Tower can still do something about, so they are read first whatever else is waiting, and a filter by engine never hides one.

safetyTiming.why: Core reads no Safety timing. A Safety concern arrives with its deadline already worked out by Safety from the grace and the panic window in force, and Core's fallback deadline is that concern's own span. If Core ever needs the grace or the panic window, it reads the settings in force through Safety's settings route or safety.settings.changed@1, never a copy of the number.

settings._note: Core's settings, in the shape packages/catalog/settings.json gives every setting. The founder instructed on 15 September 2026 that open questions become admin settings, and 'who comes after the fallback' was the question this file used to answer with a null rota. Every default, bound and list length here is the integrator's proposal, with decidedBy: null. packages/engines/src/core reads the rota and the minutes in force when a concern is opened and keeps them on the concern, so a change never reaches a concern already open. GET /v1/core/settings@1 and POST /v1/core/setting-changes@1 answer through packages/engines/src/settings. No Core setting waits on a clinical review, so there is no review route.
settings._postsNote: Each post is held by the closest role on packages/catalog/vetting.json. The desk operator is the Control Tower operator, who dispatches nurses, triages incidents and escalates. The on-call nurse lead is a registered nurse: leading is who holds the post this week, not a role anybody is vetted into. The Head of Operations had no role on the register until 15 September 2026 — internal admin staff decide the catalogue, finance, growth and vetting, and the Control Tower operator is the desk itself — so the post was skipped rather than handed to somebody else. The register now holds head-of-operations, proposed in packages/catalog/vetting-proposals.json, and the post names it; the defaults' second version gives it weekday office hours. The on-call nurse lead rotates weekly between people. Who holds a post is never in a contract, and the settings shape has no way yet for an admin to assign a person to a post, so the names stay open.
settings.heading: Core escalation
settings.intro: Who a concern nobody has taken on goes to after its fallback, when each post is on duty, and how long each post holds it before the next.

items.label: Escalation rota
items.help: Which posts an unacknowledged concern goes to after its fallback, in what order, and in which hours each post is on duty.

mustCover.why: The desk is staffed from six in the morning to ten at night, every day of the week.
A nurse lead is on call around the clock, so no hour of the week is left without a post a concern can reach.

default.proposedBecause: Two desk shifts of eight hours from six to ten, so the desk hears a concern first through the day; a nurse lead on call around the clock, so a concern at two in the morning reaches a clinician instead of an empty desk; and the Head of Operations last, in office hours on weekdays, because the Head of Operations is on the vetting register now and is an office post rather than an on-call one. Outside those hours a concern that has passed the nurse lead is exhausted rather than handed to somebody who is not on, exactly as it was before the post was held.

guardrail.statement: No hour of the week is left without a post a concern can reach: the on-call nurse lead covers every hour of every day, and the desk covers six in the morning to ten at night.

items.appliesTo: A change applies to concerns opened after it. A concern already open keeps the rota it was opened under, whichever rung it has reached.

items.label: Minutes at each rung of the rota
items.help: How long each post holds an unacknowledged concern before it goes to the next post, rung one first.

default.proposedBecause: The desk is at its screen and answers or passes a concern on in five minutes. The nurse lead is on call rather than at a desk, and ten more minutes is time to see the page, step away from a patient and ring in, so a concern nobody has taken on reaches the last post a quarter of an hour after it reached the desk.

lowest.proposedBecause: A minute is the least time in which somebody can see a concern and press acknowledge. Anything shorter moves a concern on before a person could have taken it.

highest.proposedBecause: An hour at one post is the longest a concern nobody has taken on may wait before somebody with more authority hears of it. Longer, and a concern raised at the start of a shift waits most of a morning to reach the last post.

lowest.proposedBecause: One time for every post but the last: the rota has three posts, and the last has no post after it to hand a concern to.

highest.proposedBecause: As many as the lowest: a time for a post that is not on the rota is a number nothing reads, and a post without one is a rung with no deadline.

guardrail.statement: Every post but the last has a time of its own, of at least a minute and at most an hour, so a concern never sits at a post for nothing and never waits more than an hour to go up.

items.appliesTo: A change applies to concerns opened after it. A concern already open keeps the minutes it was opened under, whichever rung it has reached.

items.label: Longest audit export
items.help: The longest period, in days, GET /v1/core/audit-exports@1 may export in one call.

default.proposedBecause: A month is enough for a routine review and short of ever reading as a copy of the whole trail taken in one call, which is exactly what range-too-wide exists to refuse.

lowest.proposedBecause: A day is the narrowest period an export can honestly cover; a bound of nought would refuse every export ever asked for.

highest.proposedBecause: Three months covers a quarterly review without an admin ever widening the bound into a copy of the whole trail.

items.appliesTo: A change applies to an export requested after it. An export already returned keeps the entries it read.

changelog.why: The rota the closed loop had no answer for, proposed as settings under the founder's instruction of 15 September 2026, with nobody's decision beside it yet.

The Head of Operations post was held by no role, so it had no hours and every concern that reached it was skipped. The Head of Operations joined the vetting register on 15 September 2026 and holds the post now, so the post is given weekday office hours, proposed with nobody's decision beside them. The minutes are unchanged: the rota still has three posts, and the last is given the concern's own span.

GET /v1/core/audit-exports@1 was declared with a refusal for a range that is too wide and no bound to refuse against. The founder's instruction of 15 September 2026 turns an open question like this one into a setting rather than a number typed into the route; this is that setting, proposed with nobody's decision beside it yet.

preview._note: The Control Tower's concerns in the web preview. Nothing here is a real concern and nobody here is on call. Each is opened some minutes before the preview first reads it, under the rota in force at that moment, and moved by the same arithmetic the engine uses up to now, so where each one is, and when it moves up, cannot disagree with the rules. Minutes are offsets from the moment the Control Tower is opened, so the preview never goes stale.

screen.heading: Concerns on the escalation rota
screen.intro: Every open concern, who holds it now, which rung of the rota it has reached and when it moves up if nobody takes it on. The ones nobody is left to escalate to come first.
screen.preview: This preview holds these concerns in this tab's memory. Nobody is paged, no phone rings and nobody is on call.
screen.count: {open} open · {exhausted} with nobody left to escalate to
screen.withOwner: With its owner, before the rota
screen.withFallback: With its fallback, before the rota
screen.everyPost: A panic: every post on duty was alerted at once
screen.movesUp: Moves up at {at} unless somebody takes it on
screen.lastRung: Nobody comes after this. Not taken on by {at}, it has nobody left to escalate to
screen.exhausted: Exhausted at {at}. Nobody is left to escalate to, and it stays here, first, until somebody closes it with an outcome.
screen.skippedOffDuty: {post} was not on duty at {at}, so it went to the next post.
screen.skippedNoRole: {post} is held by no role on the vetting register, so it went to the next post.
screen.postsHeading: Who holds each post of the rota in force
screen.postNotHeld: {post} · held by no role on the vetting register
screen.closed: {loopRef} was closed at {at}: {outcome}. Nothing was sent to anybody, and this preview keeps the close in this tab's memory.
screen.closeNotYours: Closing a concern is for the roles its close route admits, and this workspace's role is not one of them.
